documents.title: Guidelines for Teaching and Learning with AI (PDF)
documents.summary: Guidelines from the AI Implementation Workgroup that encourage faculty to explore AI while leaving the extent to each instructor. They ask for a syllabus AI statement and give three sample policies, and they route misconduct through the honor code.
documents.stance_why: Faculty 'have the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI tools', and the document offers 'permissive, hybrid, and restrictive' sample statements, so it sets no single stance and lists tiers.

units.why: The guidelines open by stating purpose and scope for faculty, students and staff, setting an institution-level framework: 'clear and practical guidance for faculty, students, and staff'.
units.anchor: clear and practical guidance for faculty, students, and staff
units.frag_end: ethical, and supportive environment for AI use in education.

units.why: Principle 1 says 'Faculty are encouraged to explore and integrate AI tools', which is a default of encouraging AI use (P02), addressed to instructors.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to explore and integrate AI tools

units.why: Principle 2 requires AI use to respect privacy and law ('comply with relevant regulations (FERPA, HIPAA, etc.)'); this fits compliance with existing law (P77) better than the privacy-tool type P50 because it names regulations.
units.anchor: comply with relevant regulations (FERPA, HIPAA, etc.)
units.frag_end: Transparency in AI applications is essential.

units.why: Principle 3 states 'Faculty have the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI tools', delegating the decision to instructors.
units.anchor: Faculty have the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI tools
units.frag_end: not be required to follow these guidelines.

units.why: Principle 4 commits that 'Comprehensive training programs and resources will continue to be provided' to faculty and students; training for students and staff fits P70.
units.anchor: Comprehensive training programs and resources will continue to be provided

units.why: The same principle says DTT 'will provide and continuously update AI training sessions' and faculty 'are encouraged to attend'; this is faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to attend these sessions

units.why: Principle 5 says feedback 'will be used to continuously improve AI initiatives', a commitment to revise over time (P54).
units.anchor: Feedback on AI tools, trainings, and resources will be used to continuously

units.why: Faculty 'should familiarize themselves with the capabilities and limitations of AI tools', which is faculty learning support/expectation (P63), not a student rule.
units.anchor: Faculty should familiarize themselves with the capabilities and limitations of AI tools

units.why: 'AI tools should be used to augment, not replace, human interaction and judgment' keeps humans as the thinkers; nearest is P32 (AI must not replace thinking), though it is not specific to students.
units.anchor: augment, not replace, human interaction and judgment
units.fit_note: Applies to all AI use, not only students' problem-solving.

units.why: Faculty 'should include a clear AI policy in their course syllabi', which is a syllabus-statement expectation (P09).
units.anchor: should include a clear AI policy in their course syllabi
units.frag_end: permissive, hybrid, and restrictive use are provided below.

units.why: The guidelines supply 'permissive, hybrid, and restrictive' sample statements, i.e. named levels of AI use (P05).
units.anchor: Sample policy statements for permissive, hybrid, and restrictive use

units.why: 'Redesign assignments to leverage AI tools where appropriate' tells faculty to rebuild assignments around AI (P35).
units.anchor: Redesign assignments to leverage AI tools where appropriate

units.why: 'design assignments to promote original student work' in light of misuse is assignment redesign (P35), here to deter misuse rather than leverage AI.
units.anchor: design assignments to promote original student work

units.why: Faculty should 'Clearly communicate expectations regarding the use of AI tools and the consequences of misuse'; P09 is the nearest communicating-expectations type, but this adds consequences.
units.anchor: Clearly communicate expectations regarding the use of AI tools
units.fit_note: Also asks to communicate consequences of misuse, not only to include a syllabus statement.

units.why: 'Academic integrity misconduct will follow existing honor code and student conduct standards' treats AI misuse under existing integrity processes (P36).
units.anchor: will follow existing honor code and student conduct standards

units.why: 'Faculty will be provided with relevant tools and trainings to detect and address potential academic misconduct' means detection tools are to be supplied (P40).
units.anchor: tools and trainings to detect and address potential academic misconduct

units.why: 'Ensure AI use complies with copyright, intellectual property, and privacy laws' is a legal-compliance rule (P77).
units.anchor: Ensure AI use complies with copyright, intellectual property, and privacy laws

units.why: 'Protect sensitive data and comply with FERPA and HIPAA regulations when using AI tools' is a data-protection rule (P50).
units.anchor: Protect sensitive data and comply with FERPA and HIPAA regulations

units.why: 'supports diversity, inclusion, and accessibility' is an ethical-use expectation; nearest is P53 though it asks for support of equity rather than naming harms.
units.anchor: Use AI tools in a manner that supports diversity, inclusion, and accessibility
units.frag_start: Use AI tools in a manner
units.fit_note: Positive equity/accessibility expectation rather than naming a harm.

units.why: 'Educate students and recommend student to attend trainings' on ethical use and bias is student AI-literacy training (P70).
units.anchor: recommend student to attend trainings that aim to educate them about the ethical use

units.why: DTT will add 'trainings and resources such as use cases, alternative assignments, and webinars'; faculty-facing institutional support (P63).
units.anchor: additional trainings and resources such as use cases, alternative assignments, and webinars
units.frag_start: The Division of Digital Transformation and Technology (DTT) will continue to

units.why: 'Faculty can coordinate with DTT to recommend or develop new training sessions' and share experience, a faculty-community support element (P63).
units.anchor: Faculty can coordinate with DTT to recommend or develop new training sessions

units.why: The permissive sample says 'This course encourages students to explore the use of Generative AI (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT for all assignments and assessments', a permit/encourage default (P02).
units.anchor: encourages students to explore the use of Generative AI (GenAI) tools

units.why: Permissive sample requires 'must be appropriately acknowledged and cited', disclosure with submission (P24).
units.anchor: Any such use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited.

units.why: 'It is each student's responsibility to assess the validity and applicability of any GenAI output' asks students to verify output (P31); the 'final responsibility' part is P29, but verification is the main content.
units.anchor: responsibility to assess the validity and applicability of any GenAI output
units.fit_note: Also says the student bears final responsibility for submitted work (P29).

units.why: 'Violations of this policy will be considered academic misconduct' classifies misuse as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Violations of this policy will be considered academic misconduct.

units.why: Hybrid sample: 'The default is that such use is disallowed unless otherwise stated' sets a fallback rule (P06).
units.anchor: The default is that such use is disallowed unless otherwise stated.

units.why: Hybrid sample says 'Certain assignments in this course will permit or even encourage' GenAI, i.e. assignment-by-assignment permission (P04).
units.anchor: Certain assignments in this course will permit or even encourage the use of

units.why: Restrictive sample: 'We specifically forbid the use of ChatGPT or any other Generative AI (GenAI) tools at all stages of the work process, including preliminary ones', a ban on graded work (P01).
units.anchor: We specifically forbid the use of ChatGPT or any other Generative AI

units.why: Restrictive sample: 'all the work students submit for this course will be their own', own-work expectation (P29).
units.anchor: all the work students submit for this course will be their own
units.frag_start: We expect that all the work

units.why: Restrictive sample asks that collaborative assignments 'list all team members who participated', an attribution rule for collaboration not about AI; no type fits.
units.anchor: we expect for the assignment to list all team members who participated
units.uncovered_note: Collaborative work must list all participating team members (a non-AI collaboration attribution rule inside the restrictive sample).

documents.title: BOV Policy 1220: Standards for the Safe Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: Board of Visitors policy setting responsible, ethical and transparent AI standards for all employees across research, teaching and administration. It covers vendor approval, data protection, research data, training and annual review.
documents.stance_why: The Board policy says it will 'Encourage innovation and experimentation in AI integration' while requiring ethics, privacy and risk controls; it sets no per-course rules, and its overall tone is supportive with safeguards.

units.why: The purpose clause sets a 'culture of integrity that ensures the responsible, ethical, and transparent use of artificial intelligence', an institution-wide framework (P56).
units.anchor: responsible, ethical, and transparent use of artificial intelligence
units.frag_start: The purpose of this policy is

units.why: The definition 'Artificial Intelligence (AI): Refers to the simulation of human intelligence processes by machines' sets what the policy covers (P61).
units.anchor: simulation of human intelligence processes by machines

units.why: Scope: the policy 'applies to all Old Dominion University employees' and covers research, education and administration; scope statement (P56).
units.anchor: applies to all Old Dominion University employees

units.why: The policy statement commits to 'Ensure Ethical Use' with 'fairness, accountability, transparency and respect for human rights', an ethics principle (P56 framework).
units.anchor: Prioritize ethical considerations and ethical use in AI deployment

units.why: 'Encourage innovation and experimentation in AI integration' is an encouraging default stance (P02).
units.anchor: Encourage innovation and experimentation in AI integration

units.why: 'Safeguard the privacy and security of individuals' data' via protection measures is a data-privacy commitment (P50).
units.anchor: Safeguard the privacy and security of individuals' data

units.why: 'Mitigate Risks' of 'biases, discrimination, and data breaches' names bias harms (P53).
units.anchor: risks associated with AI technologies, including biases, discrimination, and data breaches

units.why: 'Ensure equitable access to AI resources and opportunities for all students, faculty, and staff' is an equity commitment (P51).
units.anchor: Ensure equitable access to AI resources and opportunities

units.why: 'Leverage AI technologies to personalize learning experiences' states a positive purpose of AI in learning, closest to encouraging AI use (P02).
units.anchor: Leverage AI technologies to personalize learning experiences
units.fit_note: A purpose statement about improving learning, not a rule on students' use.

units.why: Procedure 1 requires 'a standardized and transparent approval process for the acquisition, development, and/or deployment of AI technologies', vetting of tools (P65 covers vendor review; this is the approval process).
units.anchor: standardized and transparent approval process for the acquisition, development, and/or deployment of AI
units.fit_note: Approval of AI technologies before acquisition or deployment, not only vendor contracts.

units.why: 'All AI products or outcomes generated in educational settings must be accompanied by clear and comprehensive disclaimers' about limitations and biases; nearest P31 but it binds the institution, not students.
units.anchor: must be accompanied by clear and comprehensive disclaimers
units.frag_start: All AI products or outcomes generated
units.fit_note: Requires disclaimers on AI outputs in educational settings about limits, assumptions and bias; not a student verification duty.

units.why: 'Promote transparency in AI usage by providing stakeholders with access to information about AI applications and decision-making processes' is an institutional transparency principle (P56).
units.anchor: Promote transparency in AI usage by providing stakeholders with access to information

units.why: 'assess and mitigate risks associated with third-party AI vendors' including data sharing agreements is vendor review (P65).
units.anchor: assess and mitigate risks associated with third -party AI vendors

units.why: Contracts 'should include provisions for data protection, privacy safeguards' and non-compliance clauses; vendor agreement content (P65).
units.anchor: Contracts with AI vendors should include provisions for data protection

units.why: 'Conduct regular audits and assessments' of third-party AI solutions' performance and security is monitoring of vendors (P65).
units.anchor: Conduct regular audits and assessments in collaboration with ITS

units.why: 'Implement robust data privacy and security measures to safeguard sensitive information collected or processed by AI systems' (P50).
units.anchor: robust data privacy and security measures to safeguard sensitive information

units.why: AI systems must comply with laws on student data 'including the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)', legal compliance (P77).
units.anchor: Ensure that AI systems comply with applicable laws and regulations
units.frag_end: relevant state and federal privacy laws.

units.why: Research data: 'Strengthen provisions related to data privacy and security when using AI technologies' and obtain informed consent (P62, AI in research).
units.anchor: obtaining informed consent for data collection and analysis
units.fit_note: About data privacy and consent in AI-assisted research.

units.why: 'confidential, sensitive, and other protected data are not entered into any AI research tool without proper risk analysis' restricts what is fed to AI tools; I choose P50 as data protection over P62 because the rule is about protected data.
units.anchor: not entered into any AI research tool without proper risk analysis
units.fit_note: Applies to AI research tools and protected research data.

units.why: 'Any use of AI tools in the research process using humans or animals should be disclosed in the Institutional Review Board (IRB) application' is a research-governance disclosure rule (P62).
units.anchor: should be disclosed in the Institutional Review Board (IRB) application
units.frag_start: Any use of AI tools in

units.why: Implementation includes 'training and professional development opportunities for faculty, staff, and administrators on AI ethics', plus awareness campaigns; staff training (P70, not faculty-only).
units.anchor: Provide training and professional development opportunities for faculty, staff, and administrators
units.frag_start: Training and Capacity Building: Provide training

units.why: 'Establish mechanisms for ongoing monitoring, evaluation, and review of AI initiatives' and solicit feedback is review over time (P54).
units.anchor: ongoing monitoring, evaluation, and review of AI initiatives

units.why: Partnerships clause: 'Forge partnerships with industry stakeholders, government agencies, and academic institutions' is an operational collaboration commitment with no matching type.
units.anchor: Forge partnerships with industry stakeholders, government agencies, and academic institutions
units.uncovered_note: Institution commits to partnerships and interdisciplinary AI research projects.

units.why: 'Engage students, faculty, staff, and the broader community in discussions and forums on AI ethics' is community engagement; nearest P66 (discussing AI) though institutional.
units.anchor: Engage students, faculty, staff, and the broader community in discussions and forums
units.fit_note: Institution-level community forums, not instructors explaining rules to students.

units.why: 'The specific standards to be utilized for compliance with this policy are published' on named websites; says where detailed standards are maintained (P56).
units.anchor: The specific standards to be utilized for compliance with this policy are published

units.why: 'The Division shall conduct annual reviews of this policy' sets a review cycle (P54).
units.anchor: The Division shall conduct annual reviews of this policy
